summary: Hans-Joachim Klimkeit (1939–1999) worked in religious, Iranian and Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp and doctoral supervisor Gustav Mensching, whom he succeeded at the University of Bonn, serving as Direktor from 1972.
Hans-Werbin Köhler was an Indologist. He studied under Eduard Hermann and doctoral supervisor Ernst Waldschmidt (attested 1973).

Hansa Dhammahaso works in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2017, he was attested as Director at the International Buddhist Studies College and as director at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
Hanung Kim specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. Kim earned a master's degree from Columbia University and a PhD from Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
Har Dayal (1884–1939) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Delhi (~1901–1903) and at SOAS University of London (~1927–1932).

Hara Prasad Sastri (1853–1931) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and as Joint Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).

Harald Hauptmann (1936–2018) was an archaeologist who studied at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg (Promotion), and FU Berlin (Habilitation). He held professorships at FU Berlin and Heidelberg (1980–1994), and directed the German Archaeological Institute at Istanbul (1994–2001).

Haraprasad Shastri (1853–1931) studied at Presidency College and Sanskrit College. In Indology and Buddhist studies, he was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1900–1908), head of Bengali and Sanskrit at University of Dhaka (1921–1924), and president of The Asiatic Society (~1919–1921).

Hari Damodar Velankar (1898–1967) was an Indologist who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He held posts at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944) and served as Joint Director of Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).
Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, as well as under Ramakant Tripathi and doctoral supervisor Jan Willem de Jong.

Haridas Bhattacharyya (1891–1956) worked in philosophy and religious studies. After graduating from Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, he taught at both institutions, served as Reader at the University of Dhaka (1921), and held a post at BHU (1947).
Haridas Sinharay is an Indology scholar who held a post at Central Calcutta College (attested 1970 and 1990).

Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani (1917–2001) was a linguist and Indologist. Educated at Samaldas Arts College, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, and under Muni Jinvijaya, he taught at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan and Gujarat University, and directed the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (~1973–2001).

Harjot Oberoi specializes in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University, taking up the chair for Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia in ~1987.

Harogadde Manappa Nayak (1931–2000) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1967–1991) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

Harold C. Conklin (1926–2016) worked in linguistics and anthropology. He studied at UC Berkeley and Yale University, later teaching at Columbia University (1955) and serving as professor at Yale (1962–1996) and curator at the Peabody Museum (1974–1996).

Harold Coward (born 1936) is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. After earning a PhD from McMaster University, he served as Professor at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992) and as director at the University of Victoria (~1992–2002).

Harold Hargreaves (1876–1951) was an Indologist and archaeologist. After heading Government Senior Secondary School, Amritsar (~1908–1914), he served in the Archaeological Survey of India as Superintendent (1914) and Deputy Director General (1928–1931), succeeding John Marshall in 1928.

Harold Scheub (1931–2019) studied at the University of Michigan, UCLA, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD). After posts at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he was Evjue-Bascom Professor of Humanities Emeritus at Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2008).
Harold Stewart (1916–1995) worked in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He was educated at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.
